001: Hi, Sergey! You look pale today. Is everything okay?
Hi, Anna. To be honest, my head is splitting and my throat is scratchy.
Sounds like a cold. Did you take your temperature?
Yes, last night it was thirty-seven point five.
Then you shouldn't mess around with this. Go see a doctor before it gets worse.
You're probably right. I'll book an appointment today.
002: Looks like it. My eyes are watering and my nose has been stuffy since morning.
I had the same thing in the spring. Are you taking any pills?
No, I kept thinking it would go away on its own.
Go to the pharmacy, the pharmacist can recommend a good remedy.
Thanks for the advice. I'll stop by after classes.
003: Olga, you look tired. Did you sleep well?
I barely slept. My whole side hurts, especially when I take a deep breath.
That's serious. Maybe a strain or something with your lungs?
I don't want to scare myself, but the pain hasn't gone away for two days.
Then don't put it off. Go to the clinic and get an X-ray.
You're right, better to get checked out. I'll book an appointment tomorrow morning.
004: Ivan, you're kind of sluggish today. Did you get sick?
My stomach is churning, and I'm running to the bathroom more often than usual.
Oh, that's unpleasant. What did you eat yesterday?
Shawarma from a stand near the metro. I guess it wasn't fresh.
I see, food poisoning. Drink more water and take some activated charcoal.
I already took two pills. Hopefully, I'll feel better by evening.
005: Maria, why are you rubbing your eye? Did something get in it?
I don't know, it's red and really itchy. Probably conjunctivitis.
Don't rub it with your hands, that'll only make it worse. Rinse it with chamomile.
I tried, but it didn't get any better.
Then you need eye drops. Go to the pharmacy, they have good anti-inflammatory ones.
Okay, I'll go after work. Thanks for the tip.
006: Sergey, you seem distracted. Did something happen?
Yeah, my tooth started hurting like crazy. My cheek is already swollen.
Wow, that looks like a gum abscess. You can't get by without a dentist here.
I know, but the next appointment is only in three days.
Try calling a private clinic, they usually see you right away.
Right, I'll call right now. Thanks for the tip.
007: Dmitry, you've been coughing for two weeks now. Is that normal?
I don't know, but the cough is dry and gets worse at night.
Maybe it's bronchitis? Did you see a doctor?
No, I kept hoping it would go away on its own.
You can't do that. A lingering cough is no joke. Go, they'll listen to your lungs.
You're right. I'll book an appointment with a general practitioner today.
008: Olga, you're losing your voice. Did you catch a cold?
Yeah, I froze at the bus stop yesterday, and now I can barely speak at all.
Drink warm milk with honey and stay quiet for at least a day.
Easier said than done, what about my classes?
Ask your teacher for a recording of the lecture. Your health is more important.
You're probably right. I'll rest for a day and drink tea with lemon.
009: Anna, you look exhausted. Are you okay?
My blood pressure keeps jumping, and I get dizzy with sudden movements.
That's dangerous. Did you measure your blood pressure today?
Yes, this morning it was one forty over ninety.
That's a bit high. You need to see a doctor, maybe adjust your treatment.
I booked an appointment for tomorrow. I hope it's nothing serious.
010: Ivan, you're in a bad mood today. What happened?
Yeah, my back seized up. I can't straighten up after my workout.
Probably pulled a muscle. You need rest and a warming ointment.
I tried, but the pain only gets worse.
Then you definitely need to see a doctor. Maybe it's something with your spine.
You're right, I won't play the hero. I'll book an appointment with a neurologist.
